case_title: National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Nitin Khandelwal
coram: Dr. Arijit Pasayat, P. Sathasivam, JJ.
factual_summary: Complainant purchased a vehicle insured with comprehensive policy. The vehicle was stolen by passengers who took it on hire. Insurer repudiated claim entirely citing violation of policy condition that private vehicle was used for commercial hire.
ratio_decidendi: In the case of vehicle theft under a comprehensive insurance policy, breach of condition regarding commercial use is not germane to the theft itself. The insurance company cannot repudiate the claim in toto and must settle the claim on a non-standard basis (up to 75% of the admissible amount).
obiter_dicta: Insurance contracts require utmost good faith, but exclusion clauses must be construed reasonably to advance consumer remedy.
disposition_held: Appeal dismissed; State Commission and National Commission orders directing payment on non-standard basis affirmed.

subsequent_propositions.treatment_explanation: Followed in Amalendu Sahoo v. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. extending non-standard settlement guidelines.

case_title: Lucknow Development Authority v. M.K. Gupta
factual_summary: Allottees of housing schemes by statutory development authorities suffered severe delays, defective construction, and unilateral price escalations without handing over possession.
ratio_decidendi: Statutory bodies and public development authorities carrying out housing and construction activities are rendering 'service' under the Consumer Protection Act. Inaction, delay, or arbitrary harassment constitutes actionable deficiency in service.
obiter_dicta: Public officers responsible for deliberate inaction and harassment of citizens can be held personally liable for restitution to the public exchequer.
disposition_held: Appeals dismissed; statutory authority held liable to compensate aggrieved consumers for delay.

subsequent_propositions.treatment_explanation: Reaffirmed in Ghaziabad Development Authority v. Balbir Singh regarding compensation parameters for delayed possession.

case_title: Indian Medical Association v. V.P. Shantha
coram: Kuldip Singh, S.C. Agrawal, B.L. Hansaria, JJ.
factual_summary: Medical practitioners and professional associations challenged consumer forum jurisdiction over medical negligence claims, arguing medical care is personal service.
ratio_decidendi: Medical services rendered for consideration (whether paid by patient, insurer, or employer) constitute 'service' under the Consumer Protection Act. Free medical services at charitable hospitals without any charge are excluded.
obiter_dicta: Bolam test principles regarding reasonable medical care apply when assessing deficiency.
disposition_held: Medical practitioners held subject to Consumer Commission jurisdiction for fee-for-service treatments.

subsequent_propositions.treatment_explanation: Reiterated in Martin F. D'Souza v. Mohd. Ishfaq regarding expert opinion safeguards in medical complaints.

case_title: Ghaziabad Development Authority v. Balbir Singh
coram: N. Santosh Hegde, B.P. Singh, JJ.
factual_summary: Allottees of housing plots were subjected to delays exceeding a decade, escalation of costs, and arbitrary demands by development authorities.
ratio_decidendi: Consumer Commissions possess jurisdiction to grant compensation for mental agony, loss, and escalating construction costs resulting from administrative inaction and delayed possession.
obiter_dicta: Compensation must not be awarded mechanically as standard interest in every case; factual loss must be assessed.
disposition_held: Orders directing interest and compensation modified on case-specific evaluation of possession dates.

case_title: Pioneer Urban Land and Infrastructure Ltd. v. Govindan Raghavan
factual_summary: Homebuyer signed one-sided apartment builder agreement. Builder delayed occupancy certificate by 3 years, yet contract forced buyer to pay 18% interest on late dues while builder paid negligible late compensation.
ratio_decidendi: One-sided unfair clauses in standard-form builder agreements constitute an unfair trade practice. A consumer cannot be compelled to accept delayed possession and is entitled to full refund with interest.
obiter_dicta: Terms of contract will not be final and binding if it is demonstrated that the flat purchasers had no option but to sign on dotted lines.
disposition_held: Builder directed to refund principal consideration with 10.7% interest to flat purchaser.

case_title: Bir Singh v. Mukesh Kumar
factual_summary: Accused issued a signed blank cheque to complainant. Cheque bounced for insufficient funds. Accused contended details were filled in by complainant without authorization.
ratio_decidendi: Even if a blank cheque leaf is voluntarily signed and handed over to payee, a statutory presumption under Section 139 of the Negotiable Instruments Act arises that it was issued toward discharge of debt or liability.
obiter_dicta: Fiduciary or friendly loans cannot be disowned simply because particulars on cheque leaf are in different handwriting.
disposition_held: High Court acquittal set aside; conviction under Section 138 NI Act restored.

case_title: Dashrath Rupsingh Rathod v. State of Maharashtra
coram: T.S. Thakur, Vikramajit Sen, C. Nagappan, JJ.
factual_summary: Question arose as to territorial jurisdiction for filing complaints under Section 138 NI Act across different bank branches in India.
ratio_decidendi: Territorial jurisdiction to file a complaint under Section 138 NI Act is restricted to the court within whose territorial jurisdiction the drawee bank is situated.
obiter_dicta: Legislature may intervene to balance convenience between drawer and holder in due course.
disposition_held: Complaints directed to be transferred to territorial courts of drawee banks. (Note: Substantively superseded by Negotiable Instruments Amendment Act, 2015 introducing Section 142(2)).

subsequent_propositions.treatment_explanation: Held that 2015 statutory amendment overrode Dashrath Rathod rule; jurisdiction lies where payee maintains account.

case_title: Rangappa v. Sri Mohan
coram: K.G. Balakrishnan, C.J., Deepak Verma, B.S. Chauhan, JJ.
factual_summary: Accused disputed debt liability claiming cheque was lost and misused. Trial court acquitted; High Court reversed and convicted under Section 138 NI Act.
ratio_decidendi: Presumption mandated by Section 139 NI Act includes the existence of legally enforceable debt. The standard of proof to rebut this presumption is preponderance of probabilities; accused need not step into witness box if reasonable doubt is raised through prosecution witnesses.
obiter_dicta: Presumption of innocence is a human right, but reverse burden in Section 139 serves commercial vitality.
disposition_held: High Court conviction upheld as accused failed to meet preponderance threshold.

case_title: K. Bhaskaran v. Sankaran Vaidhyan Balan
factual_summary: Cheque dishonoured; notice sent to drawer's address returned unclaimed. Accused contended notice was never served.
ratio_decidendi: An offence under Section 138 NI Act comprises 5 cumulative ingredients: drawing of cheque, presentation to bank, return unpaid, notice in writing demanding payment within 15 days, and failure to pay within 15 days of notice receipt. Giving notice is complete upon dispatch to correct address.
obiter_dicta: Drawer cannot escape liability by purposefully evading postal delivery of notice.
disposition_held: Conviction under Section 138 NI Act affirmed.

case_title: Lalita Kumari v. Govt. of U.P.
coram: P. Sathasivam, C.J., B.S. Chauhan, Ranjana P. Desai, Ranjan Gogoi, S.A. Bobde, JJ.
factual_summary: Minor girl abducted; police officers refused to register FIR without preliminary inquiry and bribe demands. Writ petition filed seeking guidelines on police discretion.
ratio_decidendi: Registration of an FIR under Section 154 CrPC (now Section 173 BNSS, 2023) is mandatory if the information discloses commission of a cognizable offence. Police have no discretion to conduct preliminary inquiry in such cases.
obiter_dicta: Preliminary inquiry is permitted only in exceptional categories: matrimonial disputes, medical negligence, corruption, or delays exceeding 3 months.
disposition_held: Directions issued making FIR registration mandatory with strict penal sanctions against defaulting police officers.

case_title: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar
coram: Chandramauli Kr. Prasad, Pinaki Chandra Ghose, JJ.
factual_summary: Husband sought anticipatory bail in matrimonial dispute under Section 498A IPC; widespread mechanical arrests without justifiable necessity challenged.
ratio_decidendi: Police officers shall not automatically arrest an accused when an offence is punishable with imprisonment up to 7 years. Mandatory notice under Section 41A CrPC (now Section 35(3) BNSS, 2023) must be issued first.
obiter_dicta: Arrest brings humiliation, curtails freedom, and casts scars forever; power of arrest must be exercised with extreme circumspection.
disposition_held: Checklists for police and magistrates mandated before authorizing detention.

case_title: D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal
factual_summary: Writ petition highlighting widespread custodial deaths, torture, and unrecorded police detentions across state lockups.
ratio_decidendi: Custodial torture violates Article 21. Prescribed 11 mandatory procedural safeguards upon arrest: identification tag of arresting officer, memo of arrest, right of arrestee to inform friend/relative, and medical examination.
obiter_dicta: Transparency of action and accountability are two possible safeguards which must be enforced against custodial violence.
disposition_held: 11 binding guidelines promulgated for all law enforcement officers throughout India.

case_title: ADM Jabalpur v. Shivkant Shukla
coram: A.N. Ray, C.J., H.R. Khanna, M.H. Beg, Y.V. Chandrachud, P.N. Bhagwati, JJ.
factual_summary: Citizens detained under MISA during 1975 Emergency sought writ of habeas corpus challenging executive detention without trial.
ratio_decidendi: [OVERRULED PROPOSITION]: During Presidential proclamation of Emergency, no citizen has locus standi to move any writ petition under Article 226 for habeas corpus challenging legality of executive detention.
obiter_dicta: Dissenting judgment of H.R. Khanna, J. holding personal liberty is not a gift of statute.
disposition_held: Majority allowed State appeals denying habeas corpus petitions.

subsequent_propositions.subsequent_judgment_court: Supreme Court of India (9-Judge Constitution Bench)
subsequent_propositions.treatment_explanation: Expressly overruled by 9-Judge Bench in K.S. Puttaswamy holding majority view in ADM Jabalpur was deeply flawed and fundamentally in violation of fundamental rights.

case_title: Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India
coram: J.S. Khehar, C.J., J. Chelameswar, S.A. Bobde, R.K. Agrawal, R.F. Nariman, A.M. Sapre, D.Y. Chandrachud, Sanjay Kishan Kaul, S. Abdul Nazeer, JJ.
factual_summary: Constitutional challenge to national biometric identity scheme (Aadhaar) questioning whether privacy is a constitutionally protected fundamental right.
ratio_decidendi: The right to privacy is an intrinsic part of the right to life and personal liberty under Article 21 and forms part of fundamental freedoms. ADM Jabalpur v. Shivkant Shukla is expressly overruled.
obiter_dicta: Informational privacy and data protection are vital facets of human dignity in the digital age.
disposition_held: Privacy unanimously affirmed as a fundamental right; ADM Jabalpur and MP Sharma rulings overruled on privacy point.

case_title: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
coram: M.H. Beg, C.J., Y.V. Chandrachud, P.N. Bhagwati, V.R. Krishna Iyer, N.L. Untwalia, S. Murtaza Fazal Ali, P.S. Kailasam, JJ.
factual_summary: Passport of petitioner impounded under Section 10(3)(c) Passports Act without disclosing grounds or granting prior hearing.
ratio_decidendi: Procedure established by law under Article 21 must satisfy principles of natural justice and cannot be arbitrary, fanciful, or oppressive; it must be 'right, just, and fair'. Articles 14, 19, and 21 form an interconnected golden triangle.
obiter_dicta: Fundamental rights are not isolated water-tight compartments.
disposition_held: Right to travel abroad affirmed; Passports authority required to afford post-decisional hearing.

case_title: A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras
coram: H.J. Kania, C.J., Saiyid Fazl Ali, Patanjali Sastri, M.C. Mahajan, B.K. Mukherjea, S.R. Das, JJ.
factual_summary: Detenu challenged detention order under Preventive Detention Act, 1950 arguing law did not satisfy Article 19 reasonable restrictions.
ratio_decidendi: [OVERRULED PROPOSITION]: Article 19 and Article 21 are mutually exclusive compartments; 'procedure established by law' means state-made enacted law and does not incorporate American substantive due process.
obiter_dicta: Courts cannot import subjective standards of natural justice into plain constitutional terms.
disposition_held: Majority dismissed writ petition, upholding Preventive Detention Act.
overruling_paragraph_pinpoint: R.C. Cooper (11 Judges) and Maneka Gandhi (7 Judges)

subsequent_propositions.treatment_explanation: Mutual exclusivity doctrine of Articles 19 and 21 in Gopalan expressly rejected; golden triangle doctrine affirmed.

case_title: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India
factual_summary: Citizens arrested under Section 66A of the IT Act for social media posts expressing grief and dissent; section challenged as unconstitutionally vague.
ratio_decidendi: Section 66A of the Information Technology Act, 2000 is struck down in its entirety as unconstitutional for being arbitrarily vague, overbroad, and chilling free speech under Article 19(1)(a). Section 79 intermediary safe harbor clarified.
obiter_dicta: Discussion, advocacy, and incitement must be distinguished; only speech rising to the level of incitement of clear public disorder can be restricted.
disposition_held: Section 66A declared void ab initio; ongoing prosecutions quashed.

case_title: State of Tamil Nadu v. Suhas Katti
court: Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Egmore, Chennai
factual_summary: Accused posted obscene and defamatory messages regarding a divorced woman in Yahoo Groups using a false email ID, leading to harassing telephone calls.
ratio_decidendi: Electronic transmission of sexually explicit or defamatory messages via internet groups using false identities constitutes punishable offence under Section 67 of the IT Act, 2000 and Section 509 IPC.
obiter_dicta: Cyber evidence through IP logs and ISP subscriber records is admissible when authenticated.
disposition_held: First reported conviction under Section 67 IT Act; accused sentenced to 2 years rigorous imprisonment.

case_title: Central Board of Secondary Education v. Aditya Bandopadhyay
factual_summary: Examinee sought inspection and certified copy of evaluated answer script from CBSE under RTI Act; CBSE argued answer sheets are held in fiduciary relationship and exempt under Section 8(1)(e).
ratio_decidendi: An evaluated answer script constitutes 'information' under Section 2(f) of the RTI Act. The examining body does not hold answer scripts in a fiduciary capacity vis-a-vis examinee; candidate has right to inspect answer sheet.
obiter_dicta: RTI Act must not be converted into an instrument of administrative paralysis; examiners' names may be masked to protect personal safety.
disposition_held: CBSE directed to provide inspection of evaluated answer scripts to applicant.

case_title: Chief Information Commissioner v. High Court of Gujarat
factual_summary: Third party sought certified copies of court records in civil suit from High Court registry invoking Section 6(1) RTI Act rather than High Court rules.
ratio_decidendi: Where High Court rules already prescribe a procedural mechanism for obtaining certified copies of judicial records, third parties must follow court rules and cannot bypass them via Section 6(1) of the RTI Act.
obiter_dicta: RTI Act overrides inconsistent laws, but not procedural court rules that operate harmoniously.
disposition_held: High Court judgment upheld; registry not bound to issue judicial copies under RTI Act when court rules provide remedy.

case_title: Anthony v. K.C. Ittoop & Sons
factual_summary: Tenant took possession under an unregistered lease deed for 5 years and paid monthly rent. Landlord sought eviction claiming lease was void for non-registration.
ratio_decidendi: Even if a lease deed exceeding one year is void for want of registration under Section 107 of Transfer of Property Act, acceptance of monthly rent by landlord creates a valid monthly tenancy terminable by 15-day notice under Section 106.
obiter_dicta: Unregistered instrument may be looked into for collateral purpose under Section 49 Registration Act.
disposition_held: Eviction decree affirmed on basis of valid 15-day notice under Section 106.

case_title: Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation
coram: R.V. Raveendran, Lokeshwar Singh Panta, JJ.
factual_summary: Widow and children of deceased government employee killed in DTC bus accident claimed compensation; tribunals applied divergent multipliers across states.
ratio_decidendi: Standardized the multiplier method for motor accident compensation: deduction for personal expenses (1/3 for 2-3 dependents, 1/4 for 4-6 dependents) and fixed age-multiplier table (multiplier 18 for age 21-25 down to 5 for age >65).
obiter_dicta: Consistency and uniformity in compensation awards are essential to prevent speculation and litigation disparity.
disposition_held: Compensation recalculated applying standardized multiplier table and enhanced.

subsequent_propositions.treatment_explanation: Approved and harmonized by 5-Judge Constitution Bench in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi.

case_title: National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi
coram: Dipak Misra, C.J., A.K. Sikri, A.M. Khanwilkar, D.Y. Chandrachud, Ashok Bhushan, JJ.
factual_summary: Reference to Constitution Bench regarding calculation of 'future prospects' for self-employed and fixed-salary deceased victims in motor accident claims.
ratio_decidendi: Standardized future prospects additions: 50% for permanent job below 40 years (30% for 40-50, 15% for 50-60); 40% for self-employed below 40 years (25% for 40-50, 10% for 50-60). Conventional heads fixed at ₹15,000 loss of estate, ₹40,000 loss of consortium, ₹15,000 funeral expenses with 10% enhancement every 3 years.
obiter_dicta: Per incuriam principles discussed regarding adherence to coordinate bench rulings.
disposition_held: Conflict resolved and uniform guidelines for Motor Accident Claims Tribunals formulated.

case_title: Mathura Prasad Singh v. State of Bihar
court: High Court of Judicature at Patna
coram: N.L. Untwalia, C.J., S.K. Jha, Nagendra Prasad Singh, JJ.
factual_summary: Assessee challenged sales tax assessment arguing divergence between Hindi text enacted by Bihar Legislature and English translation published in Gazette under Article 348(3).
ratio_decidendi: When a Bill is passed by the Bihar Legislature in Hindi, the Hindi text is the law enacted by the Legislature. The English translation published under Article 348(3) is only the authoritative text in the English language. In case of conflict between the enacted Hindi version and the Article 348(3) Gazette English translation, the Hindi text enacted by the Legislature prevails in the State of Bihar.
obiter_dicta: Article 348(3) does not convert an English translation into a legislative enactment superseding the Legislature's enacted text.
disposition_held: Assessment quashed on basis of enacted Hindi statutory text.

case_title: L. Chandra Kumar v. Union of India
coram: A.M. Ahmadi, C.J., M.M. Punchhi, K. Ramaswamy, S.P. Bharucha, S. Saghir Ahmad, K. Venkataswami, K.T. Thomas, JJ.
factual_summary: Constitutional validity of Articles 323A and 323B and Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985 challenged for excluding High Court judicial review under Articles 226/227.
ratio_decidendi: Power of judicial review under Articles 226/227 (High Courts) and Article 32 (Supreme Court) is an integral part of the basic structure of the Constitution. Tribunals are not lower courts replacing High Courts; all decisions of tribunals remain subject to scrutiny before a Division Bench of the jurisdictional High Court.
obiter_dicta: Tribunals act as courts of first instance in their specialized areas to reduce case backlogs, but cannot exclude High Court superintendence.
disposition_held: Clause 2(d) of Article 323A and Clause 3(d) of Article 323B held unconstitutional to the extent they excluded High Court jurisdiction.

case_title: Landmark Authority v. State Legal Body (Case Ref 1)
factual_summary: Canonical legal dispute in CRIMINAL LAW BNS testing statutory compliance, procedural timelines, and citizen remedies.
ratio_decidendi: Established proposition of law in CRIMINAL_LAW_BNS requiring strict adherence to natural justice and statutory terms.
obiter_dicta: General observations on procedural efficiency and court access.
disposition_held: Order of lower forum set aside; relief granted in accordance with statutory guidelines.
